header.running_head: Pledging Allegiance to the Injunctions of Islaam

Hadhrat Awf bin Maalik (RA) and his Companions pledge their allegiance to the Fundamentals of Islaam and that they Shall not Beg from People

Hadhrat Awf bin Maalik Ash'ja'ee (RA) narrates that he was with seven, eight or nine persons in the company of Rasulullaah ﷺ when he said, "Will you not pledge allegiance to the Rasool of Allaah?" When Rasulullaah ﷺ repeated this three times, they stretched out their hands and pledged their allegiance at the hands of Rasulullaah ﷺ. They then asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Now that we have pledged our allegiance, do inform us what the conditions of our pledge are." Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "You have pledged that you will worship Allaah without ascribing any partners to Him, that you will perform the five salaahs..." Rasulullaah ﷺ then whispered another condition, which was, "...that you will not ask anything from people." Hadhrat Awf bin Maalik (RA) says that he had seen persons from this group who would not even ask anyone to pass them their whip which had fallen (from their hands as they rode their animals).[^2]
Hadhrat Thowbaan (RA) pledges that he would not ask Anyone for Anything

Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once asked, "Who would like to pledge their allegiance?" Hadhrat Thowbaan (RA) who was the slave of Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Do accept our pledge of allegiance, O Rasulullaah ﷺ." Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Pledge that you would not ask anyone for anything." Hadhrat Thowbaan (RA) asked, "What will one receive for making this pledge?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "Jannah." Hadhrat Thowbaan (RA) then made this pledge with Rasulullaah ﷺ. Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) says that he saw Hadhrat Thowbaan (RA) riding amongst a large crowd in Makkah and even when his whip sometimes fell on someone's shoulders and the person would attempt to give it back to him, he would not allow it and would dismount the animal to pick it up himself.[^3] Other narrations[^4] report that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) would also not ask people to pass him his whip when it fell.
